title: The reason people lose so much strength/size on cuts
summary: Besides overly steep deficits, NH says people lose strength on cuts because they pre-emptively cut volume, sets, reps and strength work, programming their own losses. The fix: enter the cut with the same program and let performance tell you what to change; hinges hold up well while presses drop.
claims: The obvious cause of strength loss on a cut is a too-steep deficit that primes the body to shed muscle
In a deficit the body prioritizes brain, heart and organs over staying anabolic, so some muscle loss may be unavoidable
Minimizing muscle loss and maximizing fat loss on a cut or recomp depends on how well you program training
Early in a cut glycogen is not yet depleted, so big strength drops are not explained by the diet
People lose strength on cuts mainly by pre-emptively reducing volume, reps, sets and strength work: a self-fulfilling prophecy
Cutting tonnage by 30% when starting a cut programs in strength loss and destroyed work capacity
Fix: start the cut on the same program you ran at maintenance or surplus and let failure show you where to adjust
From experience deadlifts and hip hinges barely suffer in a deficit while bench and overhead press drop a lot
Do not drop to working at 60% when cutting; stay at the edge of what you can still handle
People who trust the diet more than training end up small and weak after a cut
